stories.headline: £23m plan to end corridor care in Wales by 2029
stories.body: The Welsh Government's new emergency care plan aims to end A&E corridor care by 2029. It says ambulance handovers averaged 2h24m in 2025-26, adding up to 184,850 lost crew hours.
stories.why: Handover delays keep crews off the road. This plan sets the target to judge progress against.

stories.headline: CQC upgrades SCAS leadership rating
stories.body: The CQC has moved South Central Ambulance Service's leadership rating up from inadequate to requires improvement. Inspectors praised a more stable leadership team, but there is still work to do to reach 'Good'.
stories.why: Stable leadership shapes the culture, support and morale crews feel on the road.

stories.headline: NI health staff to be balloted on strikes over pay
stories.body: Unite will ballot around 4,000 health and social care workers across 10 NHS employers from 23 Nov to 14 Dec. NI staff haven't had the 3.3% 2026-27 rise already paid in England and Wales.
stories.why: Pay parity across the four nations is still unresolved for NI staff.

stories.headline: EEAST adds military co-responders at Northwood
stories.body: Volunteers from all three Armed Forces at Northwood HQ will start answering 999 calls from early December. Existing schemes at five other sites have given 6,000+ hours and helped 2,300+ patients since January.
stories.why: Co-responders can reach patients early and support crews on scene.

stories.headline: NEAS crew based at Durham's Night Safe Hub
stories.body: Until the end of December, a NEAS crew is based at St Nic's Church on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday nights to see people on a night out. The crew still responds to 999 calls when needed.
stories.why: A good model of night-time care that helps keep people out of A&E.
